name: A Sealed Crate

faq.answer: A Sealed Crate holds lost or intercepted merchant goods recovered from wilderness routes. Handing it in keeps cargo from thieves and helps restore secure commerce.
Bandits and outlaws have recently made travel dangerous on roads and trade routes. They target caravans and couriers, leaving cargo scattered in the wilds.
faq.q: Why are trade routes being raided by bandits?

faq.answer: Trade handlers and quartermasters accept recovered crates to catalog merchant property and build stockpiles safe from roaming thieves. They compensate adventurers and scavengers who retrieve them.
Yes. Trade handlers encourage travelers to bring in any additional crates found on roads or in the wilds while bandits continue to disrupt deliveries.
faq.q: Can you bring in multiple sealed crates?

faq.answer: The crates hold recovered trade supplies and commercial cargo intercepted in transit. The courier delivering one has not opened it; it returns to trade stockpiles to limit losses to highwaymen.
faq.q: What is inside a sealed crate?

faq.answer: Crates may be found abandoned along dangerous trade routes, near bandit camps, or taken from outlaws who intercepted shipments.
faq.q: Where do these recovered crates come from?

sections.body: Highway crime has risen of late. Organized bandits and rogue thieves prey on trade routes, ambushing wagons, pack trains, and lone couriers. Their cargo is scattered across wilderness roads or carried off to outlaw camps. These raids threaten the supply lines between settlements.
sections.title: Endangered Trade Routes

sections.body: Traders and cargo handlers rely on independent adventurers to recover lost freight and keep supplies moving. Sealed crates rescued from bandits or found abandoned in the brush can be brought to trade handlers. There, the goods help secure supplies, curb illicit trade, and restore safety to regional commerce.
sections.title: Reclaiming Lost Cargo

summary: Trade handlers seek lost cargo as bandits disrupt the roads. You can recover sealed crates from the wilderness and outlaw camps to help keep supplies moving.
